claim.content: For finite random Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains constructed from coaxial cables with a binary impedance distribution (impedances $Z_a=50\Omega$ and $Z_b=93\Omega$), the Dyson singularity in the density of states at $\varepsilon=0$ (where $\varepsilon=\cos(\omega\tau)$), predicted as $\rho(\varepsilon)\sim|\varepsilon(\ln\varepsilon)^3|^{-1}$ for infinite chains with off-diagonal disorder, is replaced by a broadened peak whose width decreases with increasing chain length. Additionally, the quantisation of the topological invariant $M$ (defined as $M=2\ln((Z_1Z_3\cdots)/(Z_2Z_4\cdots))$) for a binary impedance set produces gaps immediately adjacent to $\varepsilon=0$ in finite ensembles. Numerical simulations reported in the work indicate that chain lengths of $50$ to $100$ cable sections would be required to observe a strong, narrow averaged peak near $\varepsilon=0$.

paper:933789746092572966.authors: D. M. Whittaker | Maxine M. McCarthy | Qingqing Duan
paper:933789746092572966.en_abstract: We report an experimental study of the disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, implemented in a system of coaxial cables, whose radio frequency properties map on to the SSH Hamiltonian. By measuring multiple chains with random hopping terms, we demonstrate the presence of a topologically protected state, with frequency variation of less than 0.2% over the ensemble. Connecting the ends of the chains to form loops, we observe a topological phase transition, characterised by the closure of the band gap and the appearance of states which are delocalised, despite the strong disorder.
paper:933789746092572966.en_title: Observation of a Topological Phase Transition in Random Coaxial Cable Structures with Chiral Symmetry
paper:933789746092572966.publication_name: Disordered Systems and Neural Networks _ Physics.cond-mat.dis-nn

premises.content:
A network of transmission-line sections (coaxial cables) with equal transit time $\tau$ maps one-to-one onto a real tight-binding Hamiltonian $H$ whose dimensionless eigenvalue $\varepsilon$ is related to the radio-frequency by $\varepsilon=\cos(\omega\tau)$. For a network of sites labelled $n$ connected pairwise by cable segments of impedance $Z_{nn'}$, define the site scaling factors $\sigma_{n}=\left(\sum_{n'}Z_{nn'}^{-1}\right)^{-1/2}$ with the sum over sites directly connected to $n$. The tight-binding matrix elements are
      $$
      H_{nn'}=\sigma_{n}Z_{nn'}^{-1}\sigma_{n'}.
      $$
      The scaled eigenvector components $v_n$ are related to physical voltages by $V_n=\sigma_n v_n$. This mapping preserves the chiral (sublattice) structure whenever the network connects only opposite sublattices, so coaxial cable assemblies with equal transit times realize finite real Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) Hamiltonians with experimentally tunable hopping amplitudes given by the $H_{nn'}$ above.

steps.reasoning:
State the theoretical infinite-chain prediction and its functional form: prior theoretical work on random chains with off-diagonal disorder predicts a Dyson singularity in the density of states near zero energy for infinite chains, with the asymptotic behaviour
$$
\\rho(\\varepsilon)\\sim\\bigl|\\varepsilon(\\ln\\varepsilon)^{3}\\bigr|^{-1},
$$
so that $\\rho(\\varepsilon)$ diverges as $\\varepsilon\\to0$ in the infinite-length limit. The authors attribute this functional form to the literature on off-diagonal-disorder chains dating to Dyson and subsequent works. [3-10]

Explain finite-size broadening: in finite ensembles the singularity is replaced by a broadened peak centered near $\\varepsilon=0$, and the width of this peak decreases as the chain length $N$ increases; therefore finite $N$ suppresses the true Dyson divergence into a finite, length-dependent peak.

Describe binary-impedance quantisation effects: because the experiments and corresponding simulations use only two discrete impedances ($Z_{a}$ and $Z_{b}$), the loop invariant $M$ is quantised into integer multiples of $\\ln(Z_{a}/Z_{b})$ via $M=\\tilde{M}\\ln(Z_{a}/Z_{b})$, producing gaps immediately adjacent to $\\varepsilon=0$ in finite ensembles; these gaps are visible in the measured local density-of-states spectra (for example, in the experimental spectra showing reduced density immediately beside the central region).
Fig. 2

Report numerical-estimate of required chain lengths: numerical simulations performed by the authors, using the chosen impedances $50\\,\\Omega$ and $93\\,\\Omega$, indicate that to observe a strong, narrow averaged peak near $\\varepsilon=0$ (i.e. to see a clear remnant of the Dyson singularity in ensemble-averaged data) one would require ensembles of chains of order $50$--$100$ cables in length; shorter chains (such as the $N=16$ used experimentally) instead exhibit broadened peaks and quantisation-induced gaps that mask a sharp Dyson-like singularity.

motivating_questions.content: The asymptotic random-matrix / scaling-theory predictions (Dyson singularity and associated critical statistics) apply for infinite or very large one-dimensional systems and typically assume continuous distributions of off-diagonal elements. Real experimental implementations are finite and may use discrete component values (here two impedances), which alters the local product/quotient statistics that control low-energy behaviour. Consequently it is unclear a priori whether finite-size and discretisation effects will mask the predicted singularity in the density of states. Establishing the finite-size scales required to see the Dyson-like enhancement is necessary for planning experiments and for interpreting measured broadened spectra; the numerical estimate (50–100 cables) provides that experimental scale for the present binary-impedance choice.
